minutes.summary: This was a routine School Committee meeting covering reports, several no-discussion consent votes, and two substantive items: authorization to apply for two state grants (an IT/cybersecurity grant and a multi-year DESE early-literacy PRISM grant with Harvard as partner), and approval to post a request for services for an engineering/feasibility assessment of Turkey Hill Elementary School to inform long-term decisions about the building. The committee also discussed FY26 budget timeline concerns tied to a possible charter compliance issue on when the final budget vote may occur, and heard reports on town pay/override pressures from the budget task force and finance committee.

what_happened.line: Committee voted to post a request for services for an engineering and feasibility assessment of Turkey Hill Elementary, to inform decisions about the building's future.
Committee authorized administration to pursue two state grants: a cybersecurity/IT grant and a multi-year DESE early-literacy grant partnered with Harvard.
The chair flagged a possible charter compliance issue over the timing of the FY26 budget's final vote; no action was taken.
The finance committee reported transferring funds to keep a MART transportation program running as its grant runs out, and noted a budget line running in deficit with the cause unexplained.
A special town meeting warrant article will seek a supplemental appropriation to the schools tied to Chapter 70 aid coming in above what was budgeted.

why_it_matters: The Turkey Hill assessment is a first step toward any future decision on repairing, renovating or replacing the building, funded from the prior year's capital plan.
